messages:
Aisha: Quick summary of today's KV-cache quant sweep: ran FP8-KV, INT8-KV, GPTQ (AWQ) variants against baseline fp16 on llama-13b-v2 serving profile. Collected mem, p50/p95 token latency, and QA F1 on our eval set. Posting raw notes and config snippets here so we can triage next steps.

Tom: awesome — did you test both warm and cold cache?

Aisha: yes. Warm = prefilled KV cache for typical convo length (avg 512 tokens). Cold = empty KV, first request includes full attention compute. Results below.

Diego: curious about batch sizing and concurrency during runs? those change latency a lot.

Aisha: run parameters: 
```
MODEL=llama-13b-v2
BATCH=1
CONCURRENCY=4
SEQ=2048
PROMPT_DIST=prod-like
WARM_PREFILL=512
TARGETS=(fp16 fp8-kv int8-kv gptq-awq)
run_bench.sh --model $MODEL --seq $SEQ --concurrency $CONCURRENCY --batch $BATCH
```

Sana: can you paste the perf table? even roughs are fine. :eyes:

Aisha: perf table (median of 5 runs):
- fp16 baseline: mem=24.8GB, p50=18ms/token, p95=42ms/token, QA-F1=78.9
- fp8-kv: mem=18.2GB (-26.6%), p50=20ms/token (+11%), p95=48ms/token (+14%), QA-F1=78.6 (-0.3)
- int8-kv: mem=15.6GB (-37.1%), p50=22ms/token (+22%), p95=55ms/token (+31%), QA-F1=78.4 (-0.5)
- gptq-awq: mem=13.9GB (-44.0%), p50=23ms/token (+28%), p95=60ms/token (+43%), QA-F1=77.9 (-1.0)

Diego: interesting — big memory wins for int8/gptq but latency regresses. Did you try using smaller KV tile size for AWQ to see latency impact?

Aisha: yep, microprobe of AWQ tile 64->128 reduces p95 by ~6% but memory increases by ~2GB. Tradeoff looks tunable.

Sana: any difference in warm vs cold?

Aisha: warm vs cold: cold startup penalty dominates for fp16/fp8 (first request extra ~150-300ms). With int8/gptq cold penalty larger because we load and decompress quant params into CPU/GPU; warm p50 gaps are smaller but still present.

Tom: what about quality regressions by prompt type? hallucination-sensitive QA vs summarization?

Aisha: split QA: closed-book fact QA shows ~0.2-0.8 drop depending on quant; long-form summarization shows almost no measurable change (<0.1). So regressions concentrated on factual recall tasks.

ml-ci-bot: benchmark run 1768723456 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/bench/1768723456/{profiles,logs,kv-dumps}. Link: https://s3.redwood/bench/1768723456

Diego: did you run token-level error analysis? which layers contribute most to F1 drop?

Aisha: quick layer-wise diff (approx): top 6 transformer layers show most divergence post-quant; INT8 and AWQ amplify attention score noise in those layers. Next step: per-layer selective keep-fp16 (FP32 for layernorm and top-6) looks promising in literature.

Sana: operationally, if customers want low mem and tolerable latency, maybe offer: gptq-awq for cold-sleep-evict workloads but with autoscale; int8-kv for heavy-batch offline inference; fp8-kv for low-latency online with reduced mem. Thoughts?

Tom: agree. Also add an A/B rollout: start with 1% traffic to int8-kv with real traffic eval hook checking QA-F1 and latency SLOs. If delta <0.6 and p95 <1.2x baseline, expand.

Diego: can we add hybrid profile script to the repo? e.g., selective_fp_layers=[10,11,12] to force those layers to fp16. I'll draft.

Aisha: thanks — I'll upload config and raw logs to the bench folder and queue an automated sweep with hybrid configs. Also flagging for infra: we might need different kernel selection for AWQ on A100 vs H100.

Sana: +1 on kernel differences. tagging @infra-team in a follow-up thread.

Tom: good thread. next action items: 1) Diego draft hybrid layer config, 2) Aisha run 3x hybrid sweeps (tile sizes 64/128/256), 3) Sana prepare canary rollout plan.

Aisha: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
